paper.title: RFC 4648: The Base16, Base32, and Base64 Data Encodings

program.how: written for ounce-core from the RFC's description of the bit grouping and padding; no third-party code copied (the RFC's own C implementation in section 11 was not used)
program.target: static freestanding aarch64 Linux ELF, run with `ounce-core run-elf`

claims_checked: The Base64, Base64url, Base32 and Base32-hex alphabets built by rule equal Tables 1 to 4 of the RFC (4 of 4)

All 28 test vectors of section 10 (Base64, Base32, Base32-hex, Base16; the inputs "", f, fo, foo, foob, fooba, foobar) encode to the published strings (28 of 28) and decode back to the inputs (28 of 28)
The three Base64 worked examples of section 9 (0x14fb9c03d97e, 0x14fb9c03d9, 0x14fb9c03 -> FPucA9l+, FPucA9k=, FPucAw==) (3 of 3)

expected_values_source.what: the alphabet tables (section 4 to 7), the worked examples (section 9) and the test vectors (section 10) of RFC 4648; vectors.inc is generated from the fetched RFC text by a script, not typed
expected_values_source.note: the Base64url table in the RFC text shows its last two characters as '- (minus)' and '_ (underline)'; those two were set by hand in the generator

negative_control: built with -DNEG=1 (pad with '.' instead of '='), 14 of the 28 encodings are wrong (the encode counts drop to base64 3/7, base32 2/7, base32hex 2/7), 2 of the 3 worked examples fail and the program exits 1; with -DNEG=2 (value 62 is '-' instead of '+') the alphabet comparison and one worked example fail
not_checked: the RFC's rules for rejecting non-alphabet characters, line breaks and non-canonical padding bits (only valid inputs are decoded)
the 'canonical encoding' discussion of section 3.5 and the security considerations
speed (emulator run time says nothing about real hardware)
Tier-4 and native ARM64 execution (the native comparison is x86-64)
what_a_pass_means: this program, run on ounce-core, reproduces the RFC's published encodings of the section 10 vectors and section 9 examples in both directions. It does not show that the encoder handles every input.
